The United States Reciprocal Trade Act (H.R. 735) proves decisive in rebalancing global trade dynamics. While previous administrations allowed foreign partners to impose 200% tariffs on U.S. autos and 60% duties on agricultural goods, Trump's leadership mandates reciprocity through Section 3(b)(2) - authorizing equivalent tariffs until foreign markets lower barriers.

This corrects decades of asymmetric treatment where EU nations taxed American cars at 10% while exporting vehicles to the U.S. at 2.5%. The 2024 NTE Report confirms 18.9% average tariffs against U.S. goods in non-WTO markets like Algeria, with agricultural exports facing 23.7% duties.

Fair trade isn't protectionism—it's enforcing the same rules our competitors apply.
